text:
mike: Quick follow-up from the GQA/MQA RFC meeting — ran into a few production edge cases I want to capture.
anita: ok drop them here. short bullets pls :+1:
yash: TL;DR of what we saw in prod load test: MQA kernels blow up memory when batch_size small + long seq due to KV layout mismatch. throughput worse than baseline for batch=1 on A100.
sara: can you paste a short log snippet?
mike: sure

[perf] model=redwood-v1 seq=4096 batch=1 heads=32 head_dim=64 kernel=fast_mqa mem_peak=23.1GB p95=842ms
[fallback] switched to ref_attn kernel seq=4096 batch=1 p95=490ms mem=12.7GB

clare: whoa that's the reverse of expected. why did fast_mqa use more memory?
yash: implementation detail: our MQA fused kernel expects packed KV layout with grouped head dims (head_dim multiple of 128); on small batches we allocate an intermediate packed buffer proportional to seq*group_size which spikes.
anita: so the two dimensions to consider: batch_size and seq_len, but also head_dim alignment and quantization path.
mike: right. also found incompatibility with rotary + grouped queries when we use local-relative offsets — causes extra transpose and copy.
sara: implications for kernel selection heuristics?
mike: propose a hybrid fallback heuristic:
```
if (kernel_available("mqa_fused") && head_dim % 128 == 0) {
  if (batch_size >= 4) choose mqa_fused;
  else if (seq_len <= 1024) choose mqa_fused;
  else choose gqa_ref;
} else choose gqa_ref;
```
This keeps MQA for throughput-heavy workloads but avoids the mem blowup for batch=1 long-seq.
yash: add constraint for quantized models: if quant_mode in [int8, nf4] and kernel lacks fused-quant path -> prefer gqa_ref.
clare: we should also guard for KV-cache reuse: if request is incremental (streaming) and we have per-token reuse, MQA's re-packing kills latency. prefer streaming-optimized gqa.
deploy-bot: reminder: any kernel behavioral change needs a canary rollout + fallback + observability metric.
sara: speaking of observability, we need these per-request labels: chosen_kernel, kernel_version, seq_len, batch_size, head_dim, quant_mode, kv_cache_hit(boolean), fallback_reason.
anita: and record memory_peak and latency p50/p95 on the trace.
mike: agreed. other edge cases: models with grouped-query positional embeddings (custom sin/cos) sometimes require small kernel patches — fallback to scalar implementation instead of wrong results.
yash: test plan:
- microbench across HW (A100/H100/CPU) matrix for batch in [1,2,4,8] seq in [128,512,1024,4096], head_dim in [32,64,128,256], quant modes [fp16,int8]
- correctness sanity: compare logits and kv cache bytes across kernels for a seeded set
- memory check for transient allocation > 20% of baseline -> mark unsafe for canary

clare: add a synthetic streaming workload where seq grows over time to catch re-packing thrash.
sara: ops: add runtime flags:
- attn.kernel_preference: [auto, prefer_mqa, prefer_gqa]
- attn.force_kernel: [none, mqa_fused, gqa_ref]
- attn.dynamic_thresholds: json blob for batch/seq heuristics

mike: rollout plan:
1) implement metrics and runtime flags (small PR)
2) perf matrix + unit tests (CI job)
3) canary on internal dedicated pool with attn.kernel_preference=auto, collect metrics 48h
4) if safe, enable on 25% prod traffic with automatic fallback

anita: owner for 1&2? mike for heuristics, yash for kernel regression tests, sara for metrics integration, clare for streaming test harness.
yash: will start microbench infra tomorrow.
clare: will wire streaming harness this week.
sara: I'll add the observability labels and dashboard template (latency/kv_mem/kernel_choice).
mike: I'll draft a short RFC update with the new heuristics and action items.

anita: one more thought — add an opt-in 'aggressive_mqa' feature flag for customers who want throughput gamble (single model-level toggle). document risk.
mike: good call.

mike: action items summary:
- mike: RFC update + canary plan
- yash: microbench matrix + kernel tests
- sara: metrics & dashboards
- clare: streaming tests
- anita: feature flag + doc

mike: thanks all. will post follow-up PR refs once I open them.
deploy-bot: canary checklist created: /canary/1769460001
mike: closing thread for now, keep replies if you hit new edge cases.
